texts.preamble: Gopi Singh vs Delhi Administration/ on 6 October, 2020 The Court Of Shri Anil Antil Additional Sessions Judge-04, New Delhi District Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal Number : 8735/2016 Cc No. : 53/2000 U/S: : 16(1A) r/w Section 7 of P.F.A Act-1954 Gopi Singh S/o Sh. Roshan Singh, r/o Village utwara District Aligarh Uttar Pradesh. .....Appellant versus Delhi Administration/ Food Inspector, Department of Pfa, Govt of Nt of Delhi, A-20, Lawrence Road, Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 .....Respondent Appeal received by Predecessor Court on: 29.01.2016 And By this court on : 30.01.20120 Arguments concluded : 06.10.2020 Date of judgment : 06.10.2020 Appeal : Partly allowed;partly dismissed
texts.facts: where he was found selling Khoa, a food articles meant for sale for human consumption ; - that FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Yellow Chilly Powder from the vendor, to which he agreed ; - that thereafter as per the prescribed procedure under the PFA Act and Rules after giving notice to the vendor and offer towards sale price of sample to which he refused to accept, sample was then lifted ; that sample was separately packed, fastened, marked, sealed and necessary documents including Notice as per Form-VI in the presence of appellant/accused, panchnama etc was prepared at the spot ; that thereafter one counterpart of sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA ; - that vide report dated 22.11.1999, PA found the sample to be not conforming to the standards on the ground that milk fat on dried weight basis was 27.66% which was less than the prescribed minimum limit of 30% ; - that upon receipt of report, SDM/LHA directed investigation which was carried out by FI and after completion of investigation sanction under Section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 14.03.2000 alleging violation of Section 2(ia)(a),(b)(h) and (m) of PFA Act, as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(A) of PFA. Act. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 3 of 14 - that the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, hence, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with ; 4. The appellant was summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 14.03.2000 for 25.09.2000 to face trial. Gopi Singh vs Delhi Administration/ on 6 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145950077/ 2 After filing his appearance, the appellant did not opt to file an application under section 13(2) of the PFA Act thereby exercising his right to get the second counterpart of the sample analyzed from the Central Food Laboratory (CFL). 5. Thereafter matter was listed for pre-charge evidence, wherein the complainant examined PW-1 Sh. V.P.S. Chaudhary, PW2 Sh.Sanjeev Kumar Gupta and PW-3 Sh. Arun Mishra 6. On the basis of testimony of PW-1 Sh. V.P.S. Chaudhary, on 01.07.2009 charge was framed against the accused for commission of offences punishable u/s 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act for violation of Section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act alleging therein that on 05.11.1999 at about 12.30 p.m, appellant being the Vendor cum Proprietor was found carrying khoa, a milk product, meant for human consumption at Auction Site, Opposite Old Delhi Railway Station, sold for analysis approximately 750 grams of Khola lying in the tasla ( a steel vessel ) to Food Inspector Sh. V.P.S. Chaudhary, (PW1) in the presence of LHA and witnesses, it was analyzed by Director, CFL vide Certificate bearing no. PFA/Enf./2054-99 on 22.11.1999 and found that the sample does not confirm to the standard because milk fat on dry weight basis is less than the prescribed limit of 30%r was adulterated and the same was unfit for human consumption and thereby he violated the provisions of sub-clause (a) and (m) of CA no. 8735/16 Gopi Singh Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 4 of 14 Section 2(ia) of PFA Act, 1954 punishable under section 16(1)(a) of PFA Act, 1954 read with Section 7 of the PFA Act to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 6.1 During trial after the examination and detailed cross examination of PW1 Sh. V.P.S. Chaudhary ( Food Inspector), Sh. Sanjiv Kumar Gupta ( Food Inspector ) and Sh. PW3 Sh. Arun Mishra, OSD to Vice Chairman, DDA, Vikas Sadan, New Delhi, three witnesses of the prosecution, prosecution evidence was closed and matter was fixed for Statement of accused . 7. The statement of accused was recorded under section 313 Cr.PC in which accused pleaded his innocence and stated that khoa pindi was broken into pieces by hand, then put into the bottle which were not clean and dry ; both the reports of analyst are highly divergent, sample was not taken properly, he was not the owner of sample commodity and expressed his intention to lead defence evidence but no such evidence was led by him despite opportunities. The appellant has assailed the judgment and order on sentence passed by the learned trial court by urging various grounds. 1. For the reasons stated in the application, 90 days' delay in filing the appeal is condoned. 2. The respondent/accused has not challenged his conviction or the order on sentence.
texts.arguments: II) Alternatively, on the quantum of sentence, relying upon the new legislation, it was pleaded that the case of the appellant be considered sympathetically in the light of the preposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Courts pursuant to coming of new legislation that is Food Safety & Standards Act. 10. During the course of argument on 30.09.2020, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the benefit of new legislation be given to the appellant and to confirm his submissions, appellant has tender his statement in this regard and stated that he is not challenging the merits of the case/ conviction decided by the learned trial court vide judgment dated 22.08.2016 and confining his appeal limited to the quantum of sentence only awarded to him vide order dated 27.08.2016 and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him by giving him the benefit of New Legislation as FSSAI. 11. Learned counsel for the Delhi Admn./Food Department, objected to the same and submitted that according to statement of appellant, prosecution has established its case and he be sentenced CA no. 8735/16 Gopi Singh Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 6 of 14 with strict punishment in terms of old Act wherein minimum punishment is prescribed and no leniency be shown to the convict as it is a serious offence of food article / commodity 14. It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was repealed and new act had come into operation. It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that the offence for which the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the category of Substandard Food punishable under section 52 of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called FSSA) punishable upto six months and fine of Rs. 5 lacs only. CA no. 8735/16 Gopi Singh Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 7 of 14 Gopi Singh vs Delhi Administration/ on 6 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145950077/ 4 15. It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant that appellant is a man of old age, respectable person of society, has deep roots in the society, has one son and three daughters, who are marriageable, having responsibility towards his family, is working as daily wager in the fields of others to earn his livelihood, not keeping good health and has to perform his social and family duties, not involved in any other case, has furnished the details of the owner of the khoa who has given him it for sale at Delhi and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him in light of the provisions of law under the new Act. 15.1 Further case pertains to the year 1999, the appellant/accused has faced the trial almost 21 years which by itself is a sufficient punishment and the hardships faced by him caused him great mental agony, stress and rigors of trial during the said period. It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid-19 and there are chances of appellant being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to him. 15.2 In support of his submissions, learned counsel for appellant had relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177. 15.3 Per contra, learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing CA no. 8735/16 Gopi Singh Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 8 of 14 cannot be done in new Act since the definition of many offences are changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which accused is charged. Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed. Now FSSA have definition "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food". Due to this reason, the ingredients have changed and thus there is no way in which the old offences could be related to new offences. 15.6 Sub-clause (viii) of 3(zz) FSSA Act is applicable where the colouring material or the preservative other than that specified in respect there of is found in the food article and no where the colouring material exceeds the prescribed limit. 15.9 As far as the application of Nemi Chand Judgment (supra) is concerned, the same is based on the old judgment i.e. T Barai ( Supra) of Hon'ble Supreme Court. The relevant portion of the T Barai Judgment is as follows : - (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs. Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus : - "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an ofence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs. Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 KB 518: 156 LT 194" - In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage : CA no. 8735/16 Gopi Singh Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 10 of 14 - If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act." - Morevoer, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : - To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases. Gopi Singh vs Delhi Administration/ on 6 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145950077/ 6 Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's Case ( supra ) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long pending court cases filed under old PFA Act mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine CA no. 8735/16 Gopi Singh Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 11 of 14 only. - 16. Thus analysing the facts of the case, and taking note of the fact that accused has faced the trial of almost 21 years ; and also the fact that special circumstances exists due to outbreak of Covid 19 ; in back ground of the above cited judgment and the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi titled as GNCT Vs. Jagdish Tyagi dated 11.10.2017 in my view the convict/ appellant is entitled to the benefit of new legislation. G. That no such similar or other petition has been filed either before this Hon'ble Court or before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India." 3. Learned APP for the State submitted that in decision reported as Mithlesh vs. State of NCT of Delhi (2014) 123 SCC 423, the Apex Court refused to further reduce the sentence observing that it was a case of food adulteration and there was no special circumstance warranting reducing the sentence below the minimum, especially when the High Court had already shown benevolence by reducing the sentence from one year to three months. Mr.K.K.Manan, Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent has submitted that the case of the respondent is squarely covered by this recent decision of the Supreme Court in the case Nemi CA no. 8735/16 Gopi Singh Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 18 of 14 Chand vs. State of Rajasthan II (2016) CCR 15 (SC). learned ASJ has rightly held it to be an offence punishable under Section 59(i) of FSSA Act for the purpose of awarding the punishment and no minimum sentence is prescribed for the above said offence. 5. Learned APP for the State fairly concedes that in the grounds of appeal there is no challenge to the finding of the learned ASJ that Dal Arhar coloured with synthetic colour "Tartrazine" is termed as "unsafe food" in terms of Sec.3(zz) (vii) of FSSA Act punishable under Section 59(i) of FSSA and no minimum sentence is prescribed there under. 7. After placing reliance on the decision of the Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's case (supra), the learned ASJ arrived at the conclusion that adding colour to the food article i.e. Dal Arhar in the instant case, which was earlier punishable under Section 16(1A) of PFA Act has to be considered an offence punishable under Section 59(i) of FSSA, the sentence may extend to six months and also with fine which may extend to `1 lakh. 8. The case of the appellant is squarely covered by the decision of the CA no. 8735/16 Gopi Singh Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 19 of 14 Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's case (supra). Since no minimum sentence is prescribed under Section 59(i) of FSSA, the findings given by learned Gopi Singh vs Delhi Administration/ on 6 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145950077/ 10 ASJ and sentence awarded to the appellant, therefore, cannot be faulted.
